Triage first-touch (bare-card sweep): queued `pm:queue`, **Bug + `priority:p0`**, `domain:engine` (lands in `packages/objectql/src/registry.ts`).

p0 rationale: this is the measured mechanism behind cloud#1555 — a hosted environment whose bootstrap outgrows the 20s request waiter becomes **permanently unservable with no error anywhere**, purely by accumulating metadata; production is at 134s today. Quadratic curve pinned to R²=0.994 with a CPU profile naming the loop. Queue-jump is priority, not exemption — claim protocol and the registry file's in-flight neighbours still apply.

Fix per the card's direction: a short-name→FQN index `Map` maintained beside `objectContributors` in register/unregister, preserving the ambiguity warning via per-name match arrays. The two properties the card names are the required pins: lookup independent of registration order, and `unregisterObject` keeping both maps in step (the registry.ts:2350 extraction note is the contract — a second index is exactly where read/removal could disagree). Acceptance: the seven call sites go O(1); a scaling test (or the cloud rig re-run, stated which) shows the bootstrap curve flatten.

Maintainer ruling (2026-08-22, verbatim): 「#10945 判了 p0:注册表短名查找全表扫描 ⇒ boot 随存量元数据二次方增长,就是 cloud#1555『134s bootstrap vs 20s waiter、环境永久打不开』的机制卡。修法一张索引 Map,engine 席下一轮就能派。」

Mechanism link for the record: cloud#1555's incident math — every registered object triggers short-name resolutions that each scan the whole registry, so boot cost ~O(n²) in stored metadata items; jack's environment crossed the 20s kernel waiter at ~134s bootstrap and 503'd until placement+seed fixes masked the constant factor. This card removes the QUADRATIC factor itself (one keyed index Map alongside the registry), which also shrinks every environment's cold-boot as metadata accumulates — the placement work (cloud#1521) only fixed the per-leg constant. Queued for the engine seat's next round per the ruling.

Claim: PM loop round 1

File surface: `packages/objectql/src/registry.ts` (region: `resolveObjectKey` + the register/unregister sites that must maintain the second index) (stop on breach; explain in the report)
Container & model: `M`, `mode:subagent`, `model: opus` (tier per `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --tier packages/objectql/src/registry.ts` — no path-derived mandate, floor sonnet/default opus; raised to opus, not left at floor, because the ordering/unregister invariants are a judgment face, not a gate-decided one)
Clause-②: no — an internal short-name→FQN index behind a `private` method; the accept set is unchanged and no public surface widens. Flagged for the dev: if the repair turns out to require changing what `getObject(name)` resolves to for an *ambiguous* short name in a way callers can observe, stop and report rather than deciding it.
Serial constraints cleared: `packages/objectql/src/registry.ts` has no in-flight claim and no open PR — lane has zero `pm:dispatched` cards at claim time. Last touch on the file is `9b0172d` (unrelated). Sibling cards in this batch (#11020 `packages/formula`, #10997 `driver-sql`, #11015 `metadata-protocol`/`runtime`) are package-disjoint from this surface; none of them pins registry resolution behaviour.

Premise re-verified live on `origin/main` @ `4257e4e` before dispatch: `resolveObjectKey` at `registry.ts:2366` still scans `this.objectContributors.keys()` with `parseFQN` per entry, and all seven call sites named in the card are present (1842, 2346, 2453, 2476, 2703, 3133, 3365).

## ACCEPT — PR #11102. ⏳ Landing held until CI converges (not a reservation about the work).

Reviewer of record: `domain:engine` seat, `os-zhuang`, session `session_01RfyXxZ2WPjcjhuXpiQQc3y`, round 1. Reviewed against the branch and against GitHub, not against the report.

### ⛔ First, a correction I owe — my dispatch stated a fact that was simply wrong

I told the dev that `node scripts/check-engine-split-ratio.mjs` is *"a gate matched on `packages/objectql/src/registry.ts` by exact path — this card adds lines to precisely the file that ratchet watches,"* and to treat a failure as "a real constraint on how you land the change."

**That is false.** It is the **ADR-0076 D7 commit-ratio metric** — engine-core commits that also touch other packages, over a 90-day window — currently 277/284 = 97.5%. Adding lines to `registry.ts` cannot move it. The dev caught it and said so.

This is the failure mode the dispatch protocol warns about in the other direction: a confidently-worded wrong fact in a dispatch order is exactly what a downstream agent inherits without re-checking. It is corrected here rather than only in chat so the next reader of this card does not pick it up.

⭐ **The dev also produced a genuinely reusable platform fact from it**: that gate **refuses to run in a fresh worktree** — a shallow clone whose oldest visible commit sits inside the 90-day window, where "a ratio derived here would be real, plausible and WRONG." Cleared with the remedy it prints: `git fetch --shallow-since=<window start> origin`. **Any seat opening a fresh worktree on a card carrying this gate will hit the same refusal.**

### The property everything else rests on — verified structurally, by me, on the branch

Triage named two required pins; the second (`unregisterObject` keeps both maps in step) is the one where a second index could silently drift. I checked it directly at `686d0c248` rather than reading the tests:

```
objectContributors.set    → :1379  (only site — inside openObjectEntry)
objectContributors.delete → :1401  (only site — inside closeObjectEntry)
objectContributors.clear  → :3797  (only site — index .clear() paired at :3801)
```

Every mutation of `objectContributors` sits inside a choke point that moves `objectKeysByShortName` in the same statement. **The two maps cannot drift** — that is a structural property of the diff, not an assertion about it. This is the strongest form the pin could have taken.

### The rest of the checklist

| item | verdict |
|:--|:--|
| changed files within surface | ✅ 3 — `registry.ts`, one new test, one changeset. **No sibling package touched** |
| clause ② | ✅ neither limb — `resolveObjectKey` is `private`, no exported signature or public behaviour moved |
| ACCEPT path fork (governed) | ✅ clean ⇒ ready → merge queue, ⛔ not a human-merge card |
| same-day churn | ✅ **I verified this myself**: `git log 4257e4e..ab47f697 -- packages/objectql` is **empty**, so main's advance during the run genuinely does not touch this package |
| CI | ⏳ 20/28 complete, **all success, zero failures**; Test Core 1–2, three Dogfood shards, Type Check workspace/debt, Lint & Repo Gates still `in_progress` |

### Zone 2 — my assumptions, and what measurement did to them

All three confirmed, but **assumption 2 is the one that mattered** and it was answered better than I asked. I flagged that `matches[0]` is registration-order-dependent and that an index could silently change which FQN an ambiguous short name resolves to, and asked for the choice to be pinned and called out.

The dev pinned it as an **equivalence against a re-implementation of the pre-fix scan loop, over all 24 permutations of a name set mixing plain, legacy `<ns>__<name>`, and colliding shapes** — rather than against a hand-written expectation. That is materially stronger than what I asked for: a hand-written expectation only pins what the fix's author believed, whereas the oracle reds on any drift to last-writer-wins. First-registered-wins is preserved, the ambiguity warning still names every match in registry order, and the loser stays addressable by its full key.

### Evidence quality

The ablation is three legs with **on-disk marker counts each leg** (never an editor's exit code), a `trap … EXIT INT TERM` so a foreground-cap SIGTERM could not leave the tree mutated, and a restore leg confirmed the same way. Ablated: `7 failed | 5 passed` — and broad, both the scaling pin and the structural in-step assertions, which is the right shape.

Scaling: ablated ratio **62.5** at 8× input (8× more lookups each scanning an 8× longer registry — the quadratic signature exactly) versus **5.7–11.1** with the index; big window **4,888 ms → 2.3 ms**.

⚠️ **One watch item, recorded not blocking.** The committed pin asserts `ratio < 30`, placed between the two measured populations (~2.7× above the worst healthy sample, ~2× below the ablated one). That reasoning is sound and cites an existing precedent — but it is a **timing assertion running on shared CI runners**, which are noisier than the container it was calibrated on. If it ever flakes, ⛔ the fix is not to delete or weaken it past the point of detection: it is the only assertion that tests the *shape* rather than the mechanism. Re-calibrate deliberately or move it out of the default suite.

The card's own reproduction rig lives in `objectstack-ai/cloud` and was **not** re-run — correctly declared as unreachable from the container rather than claimed. The local substitute measures the same curve.

### Next step

⛔ Not flipping to ready yet. When the remaining jobs report `completed: success` I verify the `Fixes #10945` first-line myself, flip ready → merge queue, and follow to MERGED. Any red returns this to the drive-to-green loop, not to the maintainer.
